promptHead: Athlete goal: marathon (Wexley Lakes Marathon) on Sun Oct 18 2026, race week, target under 3:45.

new.headline: Keep the volume low, rest hard, and finish the race fresh.

flags.title: Race‑day effort
flags.detail: aim for a 3:45 finish, monitor pacing and hydration. Rest and recovery: focus on sleep and post‑run nutrition. Warm‑up: keep it light and short. Strides: keep to 4 brief strides on Saturday. Shoe wear: use race shoes only for the race day.

answers.question: Is it crazy to do one more 16-miler on Wednesday so I feel ready?
answers.answer: Adding a 16‑mile run on Wednesday would throw off your taper and raise injury risk. Stick to the shorter runs you have planned and let the race be the only long effort this week.

new.analysis: The week is a race week in the taper phase, so volume is kept low and intensity minimal.  The only hard session is the short marathon‑pace tune‑up on Saturday; all other runs stay in easy zone 1–2 to preserve fresh legs.  Rest days are honored.  We keep the long run until race day and drop it from the week, so the athlete’s legs are rested and ready.  The 2‑mile Saturday session with a few strides at marathon pace gives a final taste of the pace without draining the body.  The plan follows a 80/20 rule: about 80 % easy, 20 % light quality, and the race on Sunday.  No medical issues were noted in the recap, so no safety callouts are required.  The only request to answer is the earlier question about adding a 16‑mile run this week – it is advised against as it would break the taper and add unnecessary fatigue.
